Maia for Client status reports

Prepare the client update without mixing accounts.

Maia turns permitted project records into a client-specific status draft. The engagement owner checks facts, commitments, and disclosure before sharing.

All use cases ↗

Set the client boundary

Start with the engagement's permitted records, agreed deliverables, reporting period, and approved template. Make the client identity explicit and exclude sources from other engagements.

Ask Maia to flag a source whose ownership is unclear instead of using it in the draft.

Prepare the report

Maia can summarize completed work, current work, decisions, risks, and next steps. It can link internal claims to the supplied project record and highlight conflicting dates or owners.

The draft should avoid new commitments. An internal plan is not automatically a promise to the client.

Separate delivered work from work awaiting acceptance. A team may consider a draft complete while the client still has review rights. Maia can preserve both states when the engagement records define them.

Review in the engagement channel

The engagement lead checks scope, figures, names, disclosure, and tone. Delivery owners can correct status in the thread. Only the approved client-specific draft should move to an external channel or email.

A practical example

The project plan says a workshop is Tuesday, while the latest approved Slack decision moves it to Thursday. Maia flags the conflict, marks the research deliverable complete, and asks whether an internal staffing risk belongs in the client version.

The engagement lead resolves the date and removes the internal-only detail before sharing.

Protect account separation

Use separate channels and source permissions for each engagement. Test the workflow with two clients that have similar project names. Confirm that the draft never cites or summarizes records from the other account.

Keep internal risks and client-ready risks as distinct fields. The engagement lead decides which details to disclose and how to explain them. Maia can flag the difference without making a confidentiality decision.

Archive the approved version with its reporting period. That prevents a later draft from reusing old status and gives the engagement team a clear record of what the client received.

Keep source links internal.

Common questions

Can Maia send the report to the client?

Maia can prepare the draft. External sending requires a verified connection and human review of recipient, commitments, and disclosure.

How does Maia avoid mixing clients?

Use explicit channel and source boundaries, then test them. Do not rely on naming conventions alone.

Can Maia report project health?

It can summarize supplied status and criteria. The engagement owner decides the final health label and client message.
